finalText:
40/40 pass.

## What wrong

Double rounding. `engine.js` rounded intermediate USD to cents *before* currency conversion:

```js
usd = round(usd * (1 - percent.amount), 2);   // ← discards half-cent
usd = round(usd - flat.amountUsd, 2);
const target = convert(usd, order.currency);
```

Percent coupon make sub-cent USD value. `19.98 * 0.9 = 17.982`. Engine truncate to `17.98`, then multiply by rate. Error get scaled by rate, then rounded again in target currency.

GBP example: correct `17.982 * 0.78 = 14.02596 → 14.03`. Buggy `17.98 * 0.78 = 14.0244 → 14.02`. One cent short.

## Why look flaky

Not flaky — deterministic, but sparse. Bug need **three** conditions at once:

1. Percent coupon present (flat-only never fails — `19.98 - 5` exact at 2 decimals, nothing to round away)
2. Rate ≠ 1.0 (all USD cases pass — no conversion to amplify error)
3. Discarded remainder × rate must cross target rounding boundary (EUR at 0.9 passes both baskets by luck; GBP/CAD fail both; JPY fail only 1 of 2 baskets)

That is why 30 of 40 look fine. "Stacked coupon" correlation Finance saw is real signal — percent+flat is just the combo that most often satisfy condition 1.

Every failure was **actual = expected − 1 minor unit**. Systematic undercharge, never over. Bias, not noise.

## Fix

Carry full precision through the discount chain, round once at end in target currency decimals — matches the contract the test's `referenceTotal` encode.

```js
if (percent) usd = usd * (1 - percent.amount);
if (flat)    usd = usd - flat.amountUsd;
const target = convert(usd, order.currency);
return round(target, decimalsFor(order.currency));
```

## Separate issue, untouched

No zero clamp. `FLAT15` on basket under $15 give negative total. Test matrix only exercise `FLAT5` on ~$20 baskets, so never hit. Reference implementation don't clamp either, so clamping would break test parity — needs product decision on intended behavior before changing.
